occurrences.text: MINUTES OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMPARISON PROGRAM
TECHNICAL ADVISORY GROUP
APRIL 30, 2024
Online meeting
Welcome and meeting objectives
The Technical AdvisoryGroup (TAG)of the International ComparisonProgram (ICP) held anonlinemeeting
on April 30, 2024.
The main objectives of the meeting were to update the Group on the progress of the current ICP 2021
cycle, discuss the final results of the 2021 cycle, and the plans for the release of the results, as per the
meeting agenda provided in Annex 1. In attendance were the TAG Chair, members and observers,
representatives from the Regional Implementing Agencies (RIAs), and staff from the World Bank ICP
Global Office, which serves as TAG secretariat, and other World Bank staff, as listed in Annex 2. The public
meeting documents and presentations are available on the ICP website.
Paul Schreyer, TAG Chair, welcomed all participants and provided an overview of the agenda, including
the main ICP 2021 benchmark results and estimates for more recent years, revised ICP 2017 results, 2017-
2021 time series, and non-benchmark country estimates. The Chair also highlighted the confidentiality of
all shared and presented results.
Session I: ICP 2021 cycle results
ICP 2021 results and forecasts
Marko Rissanen, World Bank, presented the ICP 2021 cycle results and PPP estimates for more recent
years. The presentation was divided into four parts: (i) general updates; (ii) data quality assurance and the
results of simulations discussed in previous TAG meetings, (iii) benchmark ICP 2021 global results; and (iv)
PPP estimates for 2022-2026 period.
On general updates, it was announced that Kosovo will be included as a benchmark country, based on
available Eurostat-OECD PPPs for householdconsumption: this increases the total number of participating
economies in the ICP 2021 cycle to 176. The outcomes of both the latest United Nations Statistical
Commission (UNSC) Session and the Governing Board meeting that took place after the previous TAG
meeting were also presented.
factors that impact the PPP revisions, namely, the national accounts expenditure revisions and their
impact on regional PPPs, population estimates revisions, the revision of Productivity Adjustment Factors
(PAFs), and the Asia and the Pacific hybrid approach to housing services.
Revised ICP 2017 – ICP 2021 PPP time series
Giovanni Tonutti, World Bank, presented the results of the time series calculations of global PPPs for the
years 2017 to 2021. The approach follows the methodology developed by Inklaar and Rao (2019), which
was adopted to estimate the global PPP time series for 2011 to 2017 during the ICP 2017 cycle. Two
methodological developments have been introduced and previously approved by the TAG in relation to
the new approach for linking the CIS region in the global comparison and the implications of the impact
of COVID-19 on expenditures for interpolating missing information.
Following these methodological considerations, results were presented with two approaches: (i)
comparing the extrapolated PPPs, currently available in the WDI database, with the estimation of
interpolated PPPs; and (ii) comparing the estimation of interpolated PPP from the basic heading level
(standard approach) to the interpolated PPPs at the GDP level only. At the aggregate level, the results
display similarities to the differences observed for the ICP 2011-2017 time series. At the country level,
while the PPP time series remains stable for most countries, there were selected cases where volatile
inflation, exchange rates, or both caused significant variations over the PPP time series as well. The impact
of changing the CIS linking approach was demonstrated to be small.
The TAG acknowledged the 2017 – 2021 time series results as plausible, yielding expected patterns and
results.
Furthermore, the revision of the 2012 – 2016 PPP series was raised in the discussion. Initially, these series
were not planned to be updated; however, since the 2017 benchmark PPPs were revised, a suggestion
was made to link the 2012 – 2016 series to the revised 2017 benchmark PPPs to ensure consistency of the
time series. The Global Office agreed to review the feasibility of revising the said historical series and
consult the TAG members as needed.
Revised ICP 2017 and ICP 2021 non-benchmark country estimates
Mizuki Yamanaka, World Bank, presented the results of non-benchmark PPP estimates based on revised
2017 and 2021 benchmark results. Firstly, the estimation methods were summarized, as follows: (i)
detailed time series estimate for countries that participated in either ICP 2017 or ICP 2021 cycle but not
for both; (ii) standard non-benchmark imputation for counties with no participation in any recent cycles;
(iii) estimation for countries that have limited participation for household consumption (HHC) only; and
(iv) extrapolation from ICP 2011 results for countries that participated in ICP 2011 only.
Following the summary of the estimation methods, a series of charts plotting the relation of GDP per
capita and price level for the non-benchmark countries, along with those of benchmark countries, were
presented for the GDP, HHC, and Actual Individual Consumption (AIC) levels to review if the estimated
results were plausible. It was summarized that, in general, imputation for GDP, AIC, and HHC are in line
with benchmark results as expected; however, it was also noted that the model returns unreliable results
for a few countries with a GDP per capita much higher or lower than any benchmark countries as they are
beyond the boundary of the model. Lastly, the non-benchmark time series estimates were deemed
plausible; however, a few cases require further review of input data for some components.
The TAG acknowledgedthedifficulty ofestimation for some cases presentedand agreed to omitestimates
for the cases where available input data returns extreme results, as the imputation would not be able to
fit them in the model in a reliable manner, or when the reliability of input data was questionable. The TAG
also recommended conducting a further review of input data for the few limited cases for detailed time
series estimates to ensure the plausibility of results. Regarding the countries with limited participation,
Eurostat suggested including Kosovo’s HHC-level data without any estimation beyond 2021. The TAG also
stressed the importance of having metadata to clarify the limitation of non-benchmark estimation, as
these results were approximations with less reliability than benchmark results.
Session II: Closing
Next steps, any other business, and closing remarks
In closing, it was noted that any remaining minor regional updates would be incorporated prior to the
release of results. The ICP Global Office will work closely with the regional implementing agencies to
release the ICP 2021 cycle results by the end of May 2024. The TAG also discussed regional release plans
and other organizational matters surrounding the release.
The planned global release assets are:
World Bank press release, blog, and social media
FAQ, factsheets, and results highlights
Interactive portal for main charts and figures
World Bank ICP Databank:
o
45 publication headings
o
16 indicator series
o
6 publication headings for PPP timeseries
– World Development Indicators (WDI) DataBank update for GDP and household consumption
PPPs.
The complete ICP 2021 cycle report is scheduled for Q3 2024.
The Chair concluded the meeting by noting the need to develop a specific research agenda for the future,
after the publication of ICP 2021 results, and reiterated the acknowledgment of the work conducted by
all ICP implementing agencies at the national, regional, and global levels in successfully concluding the
cycle.
